3: -- The visibility predicate lives only in policy info_graph_entities_select.
4: -- Application SQL must not copy it. A second copy next to RLS left the
5: -- non-inlined function in the plan (estimate 52 rows, actual 6702).
6: --
7: -- public.app_foundation_row_visible is only the role and clearance check.
8: -- PostgreSQL does not inline a SQL function whose body contains a subquery,
9: -- even after SET search_path is removed. Membership stays in the policy so
10: -- the planner can see it, and the function body stays a scalar expression
11: -- so the role check is inlined. The policy is the only caller.
12: --
13: -- COST 1 keeps each function cheap enough to inline. A row-count hint is
14: -- rejected on a function that does not return a set, so these boolean and
15: -- scalar helpers omit that hint. A set-returning signature would block
16: -- replacement of the boolean policy function and the inlining that removes
17: -- it from the plan. The functions are not marked leak-proof.
18: -- Names inside the functions are schema-qualified, so SET search_path is omitted.
